archetypes.name: harness-regression
archetypes.rationale: test-design-structure.sh shrinks from 2050 to 169 lines — risk that old structural assertions were dropped without equivalent wrapper-contract replacements
archetypes.prompt_body: The diff replaces a 2050-line structural harness with a 169-line harness. The old harness contained dozens of precise assertions: Step 0-pre parse-argv diagnostics, Step 0b route/init allowlist keys, degraded-tools gate fence shape, Step 2a SIMPLE guard ordering, postplan thin-fence case arms, Gate B bypass sentinel checks, Step 3b FINALIZE boundary, and many approval-gates/discussion-rounds reference pins. The new harness checks only: (1) every SKILL.md bash fence matches a single wrapper regex, (2) inline bash tokens are absent, (3) direct wrappers are executable and documented, (4) design-step3-state.sh is not called directly. Identify every old assertion category that is not provably covered by the new three assertions or by the plan's promised but not-yet-shown wrapper-contract tests. Flag any invariant that was in the old harness and is now silently unverified. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: regex-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: the new Python regex in assert_design_skill_bash_fences_are_wrappers is the sole gate on SKILL.md fence shape and may have edge-case gaps
archetypes.prompt_body: The new assert_design_skill_bash_fences_are_wrappers function uses a single Python regex to validate every bash fence in SKILL.md: it requires fences to match a pattern starting with a quoted ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/design/scripts/X.sh call followed by optional flag arguments or a <PUBLIC_ARGV_WORDS> placeholder. Examine the regex for false negatives (patterns that should be rejected but match) and false positives (valid patterns that are rejected). Specifically check: whether multi-line fences with continuation backslashes are correctly normalized before matching, whether the pattern allows trailing shell operators or multiple commands after normalization, whether comment-only lines could be stripped in a way that smuggles inline code, and whether the assert_no_inline_bash_tokens_in_skill_fences check is consistent with or redundant to the regex check. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: contract-migration
archetypes.rationale: over 20 inline-Bash wrapper-contract specifications in the plan must be traceable to actual new script files in the diff — gaps mean promises without enforcement
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan specifies precise behavioral contracts for about 25 new design-step*.sh wrapper scripts (pause-check ordering, sentinel placement, session-env sourcing, PPID derivation prohibition, phase-specific Step 0 behavior, etc.). The diff shows the new test harness asserting only that wrappers are executable and have sibling .md files — it does not show the wrapper-contract tests that the plan claims will replace the deleted inline harness checks. Audit whether the diff contains any new per-wrapper contract test code (e.g., in test-design-structure.sh or a new harness file), and for each major contract listed in the plan (Step 0 initial/resume phase separation, pause-before-work for post-Step-1c wrappers, Step 5c precondition guard on step-5b, Step 6 status-sidecar read before cleanup) determine whether the diff adds any enforcement mechanism or whether the contract exists only in prose. Flag architecture-level gaps where a stated invariant has no test enforcement in this diff. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
